about.title: Orinda Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a fatal collision happens on SR-24 or elsewhere in Orinda, the family left behind faces grief and paperwork at the same time. Contra Costa County recorded 78 injury collisions and one traffic death in the most recent final year, a reminder that even a quiet, small city of about 19,279 residents sees serious crashes, often clustered on Wednesday mornings when commuters head toward the SR-24 corridor. A wrongful death claim in California is separate from any criminal case and exists to help surviving family members recover financial losses and the value of what was lost personally. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise results; we simply connect grieving families with an independent attorney who can explain standing, deadlines, and what evidence matters. There's no fee unless the attorney recovers something for your family, so you can focus on your family first and the legal questions second.

whyChoose.title: Why Orinda Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Standing Rules Are Specific
items.desc: California law limits who can bring a wrongful death claim, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children before other dependents or heirs. An independent attorney can help sort out who qualifies before time and evidence slip away.

items.title: The Clock Is Short
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks further if a government entity was involved, such as a county road issue on SR-24. Acting sooner preserves options later.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond the Funeral Bill
items.desc: California allows recovery for funeral and burial costs, lost financial support the family depended on, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. An attorney can help document each category so nothing is overlooked.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Typically a surviving spouse, domestic partner, and children have the first right to file. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may qualify depending on the circumstances. An independent attorney can review your family's situation and explain where you stand.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim connected to a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal charges the driver might face. The two proceed independently, and a family can pursue a civil claim regardless of the criminal outcome. An attorney can walk you through how the two processes differ.

items.question: Does it matter that the crash happened near SR-24 in Orinda instead of a city street?
items.answer: It can matter for evidence gathering and, in some cases, jurisdiction, since state highways involve different agencies than local roads. Contra Costa County's public crash records for the SR-24 corridor may also be relevant to building the case. An independent attorney familiar with local roadways can sort out those details.

items.question: How does LawProactive get paid if we're connected with an attorney?
items.answer: LawProactive doesn't charge families anything; we're a free connection service. Attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover something for your family. This is separate from what LawProactive does, since we're not a law firm.
